accounts.name: AstraZeneca
accounts.ownership_note: CSPC-led (51%) Shijiazhuang JV; BioKangtai vaccine JV in Beijing
accounts.us_footprint_summary: AstraZeneca names existing plants in Wuxi, Taizhou, Qingdao and Beijing (Jan 2026 company statement) and R&D hubs in Shanghai and Beijing. New projects since 2025: a Beijing BioPark R&D / biotech / first-China-vaccine-plant programme (US$2.5B over five years, Mar 2025), a commercial CAR-T cell-therapy base in Shanghai Lin-gang (announced Mar 2026), and a biologics drug-substance JV with CSPC in Shijiazhuang, Hebei (Aug 2026). The company targets a China workforce above 20,000.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: A US$15B commitment through 2030 (announced Jan 2026) to upgrade the existing plants, build new sites still to be announced, and focus on cell therapy and radioconjugates. No per-site split has been published, so only the Beijing US$2.5B figure is recorded as a site-level amount. The Shijiazhuang JV will make drug substance for global markets, so it is partly an export base, not only China-for-China.
accounts.priority_reason: Largest and most diverse set of new China sites of any account (six records, three of them greenfield), with explicit cell-therapy, vaccine and biologics scope that needs MES, SCADA and CSV. Held at Tier 1 despite the Shijiazhuang JV being CSPC-led (localization risk) and the per-site budgets being undisclosed.

accounts.name: Eli Lilly
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Lilly's only China manufacturing site is the Suzhou plant (established 1996, about 500 staff per March 2026 coverage). A US$212M (CNY 1.5B) Suzhou upgrade was announced in Oct 2024. In March 2026 Lilly pledged US$3B over about ten years: more incretin-injection capacity at Suzhou, new oral solid dose capacity in Beijing, and local CDMO partnerships starting with Pharmaron. Cumulative China investment is stated as nearly US$6B.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: China-for-China localisation of GLP-1 supply, tied to the end-2025 NMPA filing for orforglipron. The US$3B total is not split by site, so per-site amounts are left blank except the Oct 2024 Suzhou upgrade.
accounts.priority_reason: Explicit, dated, multi-site GLP-1 buildout (injectable and oral solid dose) in the window, backed by a stated US$3B plan. Digitalization language was not found in the China announcements (unlike the US ones), so fit is rated from scope, not from statements.
accounts.incumbent_vendors_general: Global, not China-confirmed: Lilly US case studies and job postings reference Rockwell FactoryTalk / ControlLogix, Werum PAS-X, Emerson Syncade and DeltaV (Medium/Low). No China-site-specific incumbent evidence found.

accounts.name: Novo Nordisk
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Novo Nordisk's China production hub is Tianjin (TEDA). Three recent projects there: a sterile preparation expansion (about CNY 4B, groundbreaking 19 Mar 2024, completion 2027, isolator technology), a quality-testing laboratory (CNY 800M, MoU July 2025, completion end 2026) and a CNY 200M injection-pen production and assembly addition (June 2026). Cumulative Tianjin investment is stated to pass CNY 10B and China investment CNY 17B since 2003.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Steady capacity additions in Tianjin to localise insulin and GLP-1 injectable supply for China. Money is committed in several mid-sized tranches rather than one pledge.
accounts.priority_reason: Three concrete, dated Tianjin projects with 2026-2027 completion dates fall exactly in the design / commissioning window; isolator-based sterile filling and a new QC lab imply MES, SCADA, LIMS-adjacent and CSV work. Global Novo cost-restructuring pressure is a risk to verify.

accounts.name: Sanofi
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Sanofi runs China production in Beijing (largest insulin injection site in Asia-Pacific, established 1995), Shenzhen and Hangzhou. Its new Beijing E-Town insulin API plant (EUR 1B, groundbreaking Oct 2025) is described by the Beijing government as the first multinational biologic-API project in China.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Local insulin drug-substance production feeding the existing Beijing formulation lines, to secure supply and localise the chain. Reports mention advanced automation and digital management systems for the new plant.
accounts.priority_reason: Single large greenfield (EUR 1B, nearly 60,000 m2) in active construction with automation and digital management named in coverage. Long timeline (completion reported as 2032) means automation procurement will be staged, which lowers timing urgency.

accounts.name: Novartis
accounts.us_footprint_summary: March 2026 package of about CNY 3.3B (about US$480M at announcement): about CNY 1.5B to upgrade the Beijing Changping plant (new buildings, sterile preparation and liquid filling), CNY 1.8B jointly with partners for phase 2 of the Shanghai campus (R&D, not recorded as a manufacturing site), and a CNY 600M radioligand therapy plant in Haiyan, Zhejiang whose main construction is complete (production targeted by end-2026 subject to approvals).
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Add sterile and radioligand capacity in China for China patients, announced alongside Lilly and AstraZeneca. Haiyan is Novartis' first RLT production base in China.
accounts.priority_reason: Haiyan is in commissioning and Changping is newly announced with sterile filling scope, giving two live automation and CSV entry points with dated milestones.

accounts.name: Roche
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Roche's second China innovative-drug plant is being built in Zhangjiang, Pudong: CNY 2.04B (about US$283M at announcement), about 53 mu, 25,000 m2 building area, groundbreaking 8 May 2025, completion 2029 and commercial operation by 2031, for Vabysmo (faricimab) local production. It sits beside Roche's existing Shanghai campus.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Localise high-value ophthalmology biologics for China. The long build programme spreads the automation decisions over 2026-2029.
accounts.priority_reason: Clear greenfield biologics-style plant with a named product, but automation scope is likely contracted in 2027-2028, so urgency is lower than the Tier 1 accounts.

accounts.name: Boehringer Ingelheim
accounts.us_footprint_summary: BI's China production is at the Shanghai Zhangjiang human-pharma base, which began local production of Tradjenta (linagliptin) in Oct 2025; it also has a biopharma manufacturing facility with a filling line in Shanghai (older, undated in sources). BI plans more than CNY 5B of China R&D spending over five years.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Move from import-led supply to a localised industrial chain in Shanghai, positioning it as an Asia-Pacific supply hub.
accounts.priority_reason: Fresh production launch (Oct 2025) and a stated supply-hub ambition give a sustaining-services entry, but no investment amount, no new construction and no automation language were found.

accounts.name: Pfizer
accounts.ownership_note: Hangzhou biologics site sold to WuXi Biologics in 2021
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Pfizer's China plants are in Wuxi, Dalian and Suzhou (per a user-edited encyclopedia entry, Low confidence). In Wuxi (Pfizer Pharmaceuticals (Wuxi), established 1995) a district-government agreement was signed on 17 Oct 2025 for localised production, and a weekly magazine reports a new anti-infective line that could start production as early as Jan 2027. A Nov 2024 signing of an anti-cancer injectable (methotrexate) industrialisation project in Wuxi is also reported. Pfizer's separate US$1B China plan for 2025-2030 is R&D-focused.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Wuxi is positioned as an advanced oncology and now anti-infective sterile-injectable site. No capex amounts were disclosed.
accounts.priority_reason: Dated, in-window Wuxi line additions (2026-2027) are a real brownfield entry, but amounts, scope and the exact project (methotrexate vs anti-infective) are inconsistent across sources, so confidence is Low-Medium.

accounts.name: Bayer
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Bayer is building a consumer-health supply centre in Qidong, Jiangsu (groundbreaking 18 Oct 2024; initial investment CNY 600M, later reported as CNY 750M; completion 2026, operations from 2028; 1.4 billion oral solid dose tablets a year). Bayer's pharma plant in Beijing and supply centres elsewhere (for example Kunming) are older and not in the window.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Add local OTC / consumer-health oral solid dose capacity. Prescription-drug sales in China are under volume-based procurement pressure (Q1 2026 reporting).
accounts.priority_reason: Dated greenfield project with a 2026 completion and 2028 start of operations gives a design / build entry, but it is a consumer-health OSD plant (lower automation complexity than sterile or biologic plants).

accounts.name: Pharmaron
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Beijing-based CDMO named by Lilly (March 2026) as the first local partner for orforglipron production. Pharmaron's China sites other than Beijing could not be confirmed in this session.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Lilly states the US$200M supports Pharmaron's technology and gradually expands scale as needed. One outlet instead names WuXi STA as the US$200M partner, so the counterparty is not fully settled.
accounts.priority_reason: A named, funded, product-specific oral solid dose localisation, but the exact site, scope and whether Lilly's money is equity or capex are unverified, and Pharmaron is Chinese-owned (localization and data-security barriers).

accounts.name: WuXi Biologics
accounts.ownership_note: Separate listed company from WuXi AppTec; owns ex-Pfizer Hangzhou site
accounts.us_footprint_summary: China sites include Shanghai Fengxian (MFG17: 9,000 L expandable to 20,000 L; DP15 drug-product line GMP-released April 2026), a new Chengdu Wenjiang microbial site (95,000 m2, 15,000 L fermenter, GMP release targeted end-2026, capacity could reach 60,000 L), and Hangzhou. H1 2026 results describe accelerating capacity expansion.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Global CDMO capacity growth, with China projects running alongside Singapore, Ireland and US builds. BIOSECURE-type exposure and a strong in-house engineering culture reduce external-vendor openings.
accounts.priority_reason: Two dated China builds with 2026 milestones (Chengdu greenfield, Fengxian expansion) and clear GMP / CSV scope, but WuXi has strong internal automation teams and political risk from US policy, so fit is Moderate at best.

accounts.name: WuXi AppTec (incl. WuXi STA)
accounts.ownership_note: Separate listed company from WuXi Biologics
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Taixing, Jiangsu is the newest and largest API base (operating since Sept 2023): two new small-molecule API plants due online in 2026 and two more for oligonucleotide, peptide and PMO in 2027. Changzhou has added peptide and oligonucleotide capacity and a new Changzhou API site is reported to be starting ahead of schedule. 2026 capex guidance was raised to CNY 7.5-8.5B across all regions.
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Raised 2026 capex (company-wide, not split by site) to add drug-substance and drug-product capacity in Asia, Europe and the US.
accounts.priority_reason: Several dated China plant start-ups in 2026-2027 (peptide, oligonucleotide, API) are real commissioning and CSV needs, tempered by WuXi's in-house capability and US-policy risk.

accounts.name: Asymchem (凯莱英)
accounts.us_footprint_summary: Tianjin TJ4 hosts over 45,000 L of solid-phase peptide synthesis reactors (April 2026), planned to reach about 69,000 L by end-2026, plus a newly commissioned 6,000 m2 drug-product building for prefilled syringes and cartridges. 2025 capex was CNY 1.27B (company-wide).
accounts.investment_strategy_summary: Scale peptide, oligonucleotide and biologics CDMO services; 2026 revenue growth guided at 19-22%.
accounts.priority_reason: GLP-1 / peptide scale-up and a new sterile drug-product building are strong fits for MES, SCADA and CSV, with dated 2026 targets. Localization (domestic vendors) and customer-audit-driven vendor choice are the main risks.

sites.site_name: AstraZeneca Beijing BioPark R&D, Biotech & Vaccine Manufacturing Hub
sites.site_name_zh: 阿斯利康北京生物医药创新园（研发、生物药及疫苗制造）
sites.investment_display: US$2.5 billion over five years (Mar 2025; R&D, biotech and manufacturing combined, no split)
sites.technical_scope: Part of the US$2.5B Beijing programme announced in March 2025: AstraZeneca's sixth global strategic R&D centre in the Beijing International Pharmaceutical Innovation Park, a biotech component, and a joint venture with BioKangtai said to give AstraZeneca its first vaccine manufacturing site in China for respiratory and infectious-disease vaccines. Beijing headcount is expected to reach 1,700. Site-level building, line and timing details for the manufacturing portion were not found.

orise_fit.reason: A first China vaccine plant needs batch-record / MES scope, but the vaccine JV partner and build timing are not public.
A new vaccine and biotech GMP facility will need computerized-system validation and data integrity under NMPA GMP computerized-systems and data-integrity requirements.
Beijing is framed as a global strategic centre; digital-lab and plant data-platform needs are plausible but not stated.

sites.notes: The US$2.5B covers R&D and manufacturing together; the manufacturing share is not split and the figure is likely R&D-heavy, so it overstates plant capex in the KPI. Whether the US$2.5B is inside or on top of the later US$15B is not stated. BioKangtai JV details (site, size, timing) Unverified. In China for China. Beijing BDA incentives likely (zone clustering) but not documented. Localization / 国产替代: domestic DCS and MES vendors (SUPCON / 中控技术, Hollysys / 和利时) are often preferred; a foreign integrator must show a differentiated GMP / validation role. Data security: Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law and MLPS 2.0 (等保) constrain cross-border data flows and remote access to OT/MES systems.

sites.site_name_zh: 阿斯利康上海临港细胞治疗商业化生产与供应基地
sites.investment_display: Not disclosed (part of the US$15B China commitment)
sites.technical_scope: Commercial manufacturing and supply base for autologous CAR-T therapies (lead product AZD0120, a BCMA/CD19 dual-target CAR-T in clinical development for multiple myeloma and autoimmune disease) for China and other Asian markets, in the Lin-gang area of the Shanghai Free Trade Zone. A companion Zhangjiang innovation centre will handle early research, viral vector / plasmid development, analytical testing and clinical production. Announced 19 March 2026; groundbreaking date, capacity and schedule not found.

orise_fit.reason: Autologous cell therapy needs vein-to-vein batch tracking and electronic batch records; the base is described as end-to-end.
New GMP cell-therapy facility under Lin-gang pilot policy will need computerized-system validation and data integrity per NMPA GMP computerized-systems and data-integrity requirements.
Patient-specific supply chain and chain-of-identity data platforms are typical digitalization scope; not stated.

sites.notes: First end-to-end multinational cell-therapy capability in China, enabled by Lin-gang pilot policy for foreign-invested cell therapy. No separate budget published. Local government incentives and Lin-gang zone clustering likely but not documented. Data security: Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law and MLPS 2.0 (等保) constrain cross-border data flows and remote access to OT/MES systems.

gaps_html:
How this dashboard was built

This is the China twin of the US dashboard: same structure, filters, map logic, fit matrix and export; only the data, map and labels differ. A seed list of 45 pharma, CDMO and Chinese-pharma accounts was scored (explicit automation language, project scale, timing certainty, account risk; see china-account-tiering.csv) and only Tier 1 and Tier 2 accounts with at least one qualifying greenfield or brownfield project from Jan 2024 to today (or an announced start through 2030) were researched in depth. That gives 13 accounts and 25 site records. Research used web search over company and government announcements, trade press (Fierce Pharma, Pharma Manufacturing, BioSpectrum Asia, Yicai, China Daily) and a small number of Chinese-language government and press pages. Every record carries source links and a confidence level (High = official source; Medium = reputable trade press; Low = single or indirect source).

Currency. Original figures are kept in each record's investment text (CNY, USD or EUR as announced). All USD-equivalent values (KPIs and map shading) use one rate: 1 USD = 6.74 CNY (PBOC central parity of 8 Oct 2026 was reported as 6.7367 by a secondary source, stockwirex.com; check against CFETS before external use) and, for Sanofi's EUR 1B only, 1 EUR = 1.16 USD (approximate). USD-announced figures are not converted. Press-quoted USD amounts at announcement dates (for example US$212M for Lilly Suzhou) differ from the USD-equivalent shown because they used older rates.

Known limitations

  • No direct reading of primary pages. This build ran in a sandbox where direct page fetches were blocked, so facts come from search-result summaries. Official pages (company releases, government sites, HKEXnews) were surfaced by search but not opened; their High rating reflects the publisher, not a read-through. Treat all Medium and Low items as needing confirmation before customer use.
  • Chinese-language sources thin. The search tool returned mostly English results. Chinese government and press pages were found for Pfizer Wuxi, Novo, Roche and a few others, marked (zh). The following were not reached: cninfo.com.cn and SSE/SZSE announcements, the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, Qichacha / Tianyancha, NMPA drug-manufacturing-licence and GMP databases, EIA (环评) public notices, China Land Market, NDRC / DRC filings, public tender platforms (cebpubservice.com, ccgp.gov.cn), BOSS Zhipin / Liepin / 51job / Zhaopin job postings, ISPE / PDA China talks, and company WeChat accounts. These would be the best sources for unannounced greenfield signals and for incumbent MES / DCS names.
  • Incumbent vendors. No China-site incumbent evidence (PAS-X, Siemens, Rockwell, Emerson, Honeywell, Yokogawa, AVEVA, SUPCON, Hollysys) could be found because job-posting sites were unreachable; those fields are blank rather than inferred. Lilly's entry is the global pattern from the US data (Medium/Low).
  • Combined, non-itemised figures. AstraZeneca's US$15B (Wuxi, Taizhou, Qingdao, Beijing, new sites), Lilly's US$3B, Novartis's CNY 3.3B package (only Changping and Haiyan are plant lines) and WuXi / Asymchem group capex are not split by site; no per-site amount was invented, so the investment KPI is a floor. AstraZeneca's US$2.5B Beijing figure covers R&D, biotech and manufacturing together and inflates the KPI relative to plant capex.
  • Investment mixing. Totals combine announced commitments of different types (capex, JV, R&D) and different durations (up to ten years). Do not read the KPI as one-year spend.
  • Coordinates are city or development-zone level approximations, not site addresses.
  • Map. Province boundaries are Natural Earth 1:10m admin-1 polygons (simplified, Albers equal-area conic, embedded so the file works offline), not geoBoundaries, because the geoBoundaries file was not retrievable here. Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau and the South China Sea islands are not drawn; no account has a site in Hong Kong or Macau. Boundaries are indicative and carry no legal weight. Beijing, Tianjin and Shanghai are labelled in boxes on the right.
  • Reference files. The Downloads folder, the DACH CSV and territory plan, the EPCM project matrix and the PowerPoint brand template were not available. The tiering score therefore follows the method described in the brief and the US dashboard's priority reasons (weights: automation language 30%, scale 25%, timing 25%, risk 20%; Tier 1 ≥ 75, Tier 2 60-74, Tier 3 45-59, Tier 4 < 45), and EPCM leads (PM Group, Exyte, Jacobs) were not cross-checked. The logo and brand CSS are reused unchanged from the US file.

China-specific context to apply when qualifying deals

  • Volume-based procurement (VBP). National VBP cuts prices on off-patent and some branded drugs and constrains capex payback for generics-heavy sites (for example Bayer's Q1 2026 China results cite VBP pressure on Aspirin Cardio and Stivarga; Pfizer Wuxi injectables; BI's Tradjenta localisation). Innovative, growth products (GLP-1, biologics, cell therapy) are less exposed.
  • Localization / 国产替代. Chinese buyers and many multinational China plants prefer domestic automation vendors (SUPCON / 中控技术, Hollysys / 和利时). Position Orise on GMP validation, MES integration and global-standard data integrity rather than on DCS supply.
  • Data security. Data Security Law, Cybersecurity Law and MLPS 2.0 (等保) affect remote access, cloud hosting and cross-border data flows for foreign OT / MES vendors.
  • In China, for China. Most multinational projects (Lilly, Novo, Sanofi, Roche, Novartis) localise supply for the Chinese market; the Shijiazhuang JV and the CDMOs also serve export markets.
  • Local incentives and zone clustering. Many projects sit in development zones (BDA Yizhuang, TEDA Tianjin, Zhangjiang, Lin-gang, Suzhou, Taizhou China Medical City, Wuxi); incentives are likely but were documented only where cited.

Accounts or areas where information was notably thin or unverified

  • Pfizer Wuxi — two differing project descriptions (methotrexate injectable, Nov 2024; anti-infective line from Jan 2027), no amounts, one source is a weekly magazine (Low).
  • AstraZeneca Wuxi / Taizhou / Qingdao — placeholder expansion records only; products, scope and schedule are not published. The BioKangtai vaccine JV site is not identified.
  • Lilly Beijing OSD vs Pharmaron — may be the same project; Pharmaron's site, whether the US$200M is equity or capex, and one outlet naming WuXi STA instead are unresolved.
  • Novo Nordisk Tianjin — construction status of the sterile expansion and the QC lab not reported; pen-assembly item has only secondary coverage (Low).
  • Sanofi Beijing — completion year 2032 from one outlet; automation vendor unknown.
  • Bayer Qidong — greenfield vs brownfield unverified.
  • WuXi Biologics / WuXi AppTec / Asymchem — sources are company results and trade press; site-level capex not disclosed. Ownership: WuXi Biologics now owns the ex-Pfizer Hangzhou biologics site (2021); WuXi AppTec and WuXi Biologics are separate listed groups. Catalent is owned by Novo Holdings and has no verified in-window China project.
  • BeOne (BeiGene), Innovent, Hengrui, CSPC — large Chinese groups with expansion intent but no dated, verifiable in-window plant project found; evaluated as excluded below.
  • Multinational accounts with no qualifying China project found may still have projects that appear only in Chinese filings (EIA notices, NMPA licences, tender sites) that could not be searched here.

Accounts excluded (no qualifying China project, or Tier 3-4)

  • MSD (Merck & Co.) (Tier 3) — No qualifying project found: Hangzhou projects pre-date the window; no 2025-26 announcement in sources reviewed.
  • GSK (Tier 4) — No China manufacturing project: Tianjin site closed; China production outsourced.
  • Takeda (Tier 4) — No qualifying project found: only pre-window expansion evidence.
  • Johnson & Johnson Innovative Medicine (Tier 3) — No qualifying project found: Xi'an expansion pre-dates the window.

  • Abbott (Tier 4) — No qualifying project found: only 2011-2015 investments.
  • Fresenius Kabi (Tier 4) — No qualifying project found: only Nanchang medical-device news; Q1 2026 reports of operational hurdles in China.
  • CSL (Tier 4) — Not researched in depth: no China project found; Wuhan plasma ownership not verified.
  • Biogen (Tier 4) — No China project: no China manufacturing site found.
  • Regeneron (Tier 4) — No China project: no China manufacturing site found.
  • Porton (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no verified in-window China project; localization risk.
  • WuXi XDC (WuXi Biologics affiliate) (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no verified in-window China project in sources reviewed.
  • GenScript ProBio (Tier 4) — Tier 4: no China project found in sources reviewed.
  • Lonza (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no in-window China project; capsule business changing owner.
  • Catalent (Tier 4) — Tier 4: no China project found; ownership changed, no current China plan found.
  • Sartorius (Tier 3) — Tier 3: supplier plant; announcement pre-dates the window and status unverified.
  • Samsung Biologics (Tier 4) — No China project: no China manufacturing site.
  • BeOne Medicines (BeiGene) (Tier 2) — Tier 2 candidate but no qualifying project verified; Guangzhou expansion described only as 'planned' (SCMP 2025) and Suzhou groundbreaking undated.
  • Jiangsu Hengrui (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no named project; localization risk.
  • CSPC (Tier 3) — Tier 3: JV counted under AstraZeneca; domestic-vendor preference.
  • Innovent (Tier 3) — Tier 3: expansion evidence is a company-profile listing (Low); localization risk.
  • Sinopharm / CNBG (Tier 3) — Tier 3: restructuring news only; localization risk.
  • Sino Biopharm (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no project found; localization risk.
  • Fosun Pharma (Tier 3) — Tier 3: no in-window project found.
